newsitem.title: JAPAN: Idemitsu in talks over Australia coal stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Idemitsu in talks over Australia coal stake sale.

text.p: Oil refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Monday it was in talks to sell a portion of its interest in the Ensham coal mine in Queensland, Australia, to Japan's semi-governmental Electric Power Development Co Ltd.
Electric Power, which specialises in selling electricity to utilities, said it was interested in buying a 10 percent stake in the Ensham mine in light of expectations of growing demand for coal.
The Idemitsu group owns 95 percent of the mine, with South Korea's LG International Co Ltd, known as Lucky Goldstar, owning the remaining five percent.

Electric Power Development is currently constructing two coal-fuelled thermal reactors, with capacity of one million kilowatts (kw) and two million kw, respectively, in southern Japan. The smaller reactor is due to come on line in July 1997, and the latter around 2000 to 2001, the spokesman said.
Electric Power consumes about 11 million tonnes of coal a year at its 12 coal-fuelled thermal reactors, of which imports account for about 7.5 million tonnes.
Idemitsu Kosan owns three coal mines in Australia and imports about five to six million tonnes of coal a year.
